venues.title: All venues
venues.intro: The use cases every venue has. The venue sections below show how each venue uses them, with its own areas, categories, units and peaks.
cases: A person signs in with name and password (and two-step code); an officer is checked in as the security officer and must check in again every 15 minutes, or a SUPERVISION alarm is raised.
Counting systems send counts and moves; levels are worked out from capacity (and density); the console shows the venue map, levels, trends and warnings, and changes appear at once on every screen.
An operator reports, or a visitor uses the help page; the nearest available unit with the right skill and language is sent, or the incident waits in its priority queue.
The unit's phone shows the task with the route; the unit acknowledges, reports on scene and resolves; without an answer the task is reminded and then passed on.
A CRITICAL incident; the nearest free unit goes, units within 5 minutes are alerted, a lower-priority task may be interrupted.
A lookout goes to every unit, the search area widens, exits check people leaving; Found stops it and the person is brought to the meeting point.
When an area turns HIGH (or is about to turn CRITICAL) a unit is sent automatically; the officer approves it or rejects it as a false alarm.
An alarm or a long CRITICAL proposes an evacuation; the officer previews the plan and starts it; every unit is told which exit to use; the officer ends it.
Drafted messages for screens and PA reach the public only after an officer approves them.
Before a scheduled peak, levels start earlier and free units are placed; at shift changes a handover report is written.
Reports (busiest areas, response times) and replay of any day minute by minute.
Users and roles, the venue editor, personal-data requests.

venues.title: Airport
venues.intro: Sample International Airport: two terminals, security screening, passport control, gates, baggage claim and a rail station (16 areas, 8 units). Levels from 60, 80 and 95 %. Automatic dispatch of crowd control at HIGH or on a trend warning. Peaks: the morning check-in at 06:30 and the evening departure bank at 18:00. Shifts at 06:00, 14:00 and 22:00.
cases: Lane and door counters report SEC-1 and SEC-2; a TREND warning comes up to 10 minutes before CRITICAL; at HIGH a crowd-control unit (A01, A02, A05 or A06) is sent automatically and the units in CHECKIN-1 are told to hold the flow.
Prepare for the evening departure bank
From 17:30 the levels of Airside T1 start 10 points earlier and free units are placed at the gates; the officer watches GATE-A and GATE-B.
A SECURITY incident (CRITICAL) goes to the nearest security unit (A02 or A07); moving a unit onto the restricted apron needs an officer's approval.
Assist a passenger with reduced mobility
A PRM request (NORMAL) goes to a wheelchair unit (A04 or A08); the passenger's details are erased when it is resolved.
A LOST_PERSON report sends a lookout to every unit; units at CURB-1, CURB-2 and TRAIN check people leaving; the person is brought to ARRIVALS-1.
A MEDICAL incident (CRITICAL) goes to A03 or A08; a unit on the spot can press SOS.
A fire alarm in T1 Landside proposes evacuating that zone; the officer previews the plan (exits CURB-1, CURB-2, TRAIN, with the time to clear) and starts it.
Count passengers without counting them twice
Door counters between zones send moves; the curb and rail entrances move people from and to OUTSIDE; the count check alerts when the zones and the gates disagree.
Hand over at a shift change
At 06:00, 14:00 and 22:00 a handover report lists open incidents, lost persons and the situation.

venues.title: Stadium
venues.intro: Sample National Stadium: four stands, concourses, turnstiles, plazas and a metro station (14 areas, 6 units). Levels from 55, 80 and 95 %. Automatic dispatch at crowd pressure (CRUSH) at HIGH or on a trend warning. Peaks: gates open at 19:00, full time at 21:00. Shifts at 15:00 and 23:00.
cases: From 18:30 the outer ring's levels start earlier and stewards are placed; turnstile counters report the queues and the units at the turnstiles hold the flow when a concourse turns HIGH.
Prevent a crush at a barrier
A CRUSH incident is raised automatically at HIGH or on a trend; the area is brought up to 2 units at HIGH and 4 at CRITICAL; the officer reviews the dispatch.
Stop a fight in the stands
A FIGHT incident (CRITICAL) goes to the security units (S03 police liaison, stewards with security).
A LOST_CHILD report (CRITICAL) sends a lookout to every steward; the turnstiles and plazas check children leaving; the child is brought to PLAZA-S.
A MEDICAL incident goes to the nearest medical post (S04 east, S05 west); stewards nearby are alerted as backup.
Assist a fan with access needs
An ACCESS request goes to the access team (S06).
Empty the stadium at full time
From 20:30 the outer ring is prepared; exit flows of PLAZA-N, PLAZA-S and METRO spread the crowd; the turnstiles are the bottleneck.
An alarm proposes evacuating the stand's zone (North, South, East or West); the plan shows each group's exit and the time until the zone is clear.
A FACILITY incident (LOW: lift, toilet, light) goes to any free unit.

venues.title: Holy Mosques (Umrah)
venues.intro: Masjid al-Haram in Makkah and al-Masjid an-Nabawi in Madinah: the Mataf and its upper level, the Mas'a, the expansions, gates, courtyards and plazas (26 areas, 12 scout teams). Levels from 50, 75 and 90 %, and from people per square metre in the dense areas. Peaks at Dhuhr (12:15) and Maghrib and Isha (18:00). The two cities are not linked, so a team is never sent from one to the other.
cases: Watch the density of the Mataf and the Mas'a
Head counts and density estimates report the Mataf, its upper level and the Mas'a; the level follows people per square metre (HIGH from 4); the venue map shows the Holy Mosques live.
Control the flow at prayer times
Before Dhuhr and Maghrib the levels of Makkah (and Madinah at Dhuhr) start earlier, teams are placed at the gates, and the teams next to a HIGH area hold the flow.

A lost-pilgrim report sends a lookout to every team of that city; a team speaking the pilgrim's language (Urdu, Indonesian, Turkish, ...) is preferred; the pilgrim is brought to KA-GATE in Makkah or SALAM in Madinah.
An ELDERLY request (HIGH) goes to a team with wheelchairs (T01, T03, T08, T12).
A MEDICAL incident (CRITICAL) goes to a first-aid team (T05, T08, T14); a team can press SOS.
A CROWD incident is raised at HIGH or on a trend; the area is reinforced and the flow held at the gates; the officer reviews it.
The plan spreads the Mataf crowd over several exits (plazas and yards) and estimates the time to clear; only Makkah is planned.
Warn of heat stress in the courtyards
A weather reading gives the heat index; when the band changes an alert names the outdoor courtyards and plazas and what teams should do.
Ask for help without an app
A QR code in the area opens the help page in Arabic or English; the report becomes an incident at that area.

venues.title: Mall (the template venue)
venues.intro: City Centre Mall, the template venue: entrances, an atrium, a food court on level 1 and a cinema on level 2, joined by stairs and a lift (7 areas, 3 units). Levels from 50, 75 and 90 %. Peak at lunchtime (13:00). Shifts at 08:00 and 16:00.
cases: From 12:30 the atrium's levels start earlier and units are placed; the food court and atrium counts are watched.
A LOST_CHILD report sends a lookout; ENT-N, ENT-S and the car park check children leaving; the child is brought to the atrium.
A SECURITY incident (HIGH) goes to guard G1.
A MEDICAL incident goes to G2 (first aid).
A CLEANING incident (LOW) goes to any free unit, such as the host desk.
An alarm proposes evacuating its floor's zone; the plan uses the stairs, never the lift.
Entrance counters move people from and to OUTSIDE; the count check compares the floors with the entrances.
